name: World War II
description: The Second World War in Europe and the Pacific: the leaders, the battles, the Holocaust and the atomic bomb.

checkpoints.name: The road to war
checkpoints.note: The Treaty of Versailles and the hard interwar years leave grievances and weak democracies. Hitler builds Nazi Germany, Japan opens a full war on China in 1937, Spain falls into civil war, Kristallnacht shows the violence aimed at Germany's Jews, and at Munich Europe tries to buy peace with a neighbour's land.

checkpoints.name: Axis advances
checkpoints.note: War begins in Poland in 1939. Germany goes around the Maginot Line and overruns France, Churchill's Britain wins the air fight with Spitfires and endures the Blitz, and the Bismarck is sunk in the Atlantic. Hitler attacks Stalin's Soviet Union, and Japan's strike on Pearl Harbor brings Roosevelt's United States into a world war.

checkpoints.name: The tide turns
checkpoints.note: Midway, Stalingrad and El Alamein stop the Axis on three fronts, and at Kursk the Red Army beats the German army in open battle. Behind the lines the Holocaust reaches its height: millions are murdered at Auschwitz and other camps, and in 1943 the Jews of the Warsaw Ghetto rise in revolt.

checkpoints.name: Allied victory
checkpoints.note: Allied troops land in Normandy, helped by codebreakers such as Alan Turing and by Colossus, which read German signals. V-2 rockets fall on London and Antwerp, Germany's last offensive fails in the Ardennes, and the Red Army storms Berlin. The leaders meet at Yalta, the Manhattan Project's atomic bombs end the war in Asia, and the United Nations is founded.

checkpoints.name: Aftermath
checkpoints.note: The Nuremberg tribunal, which opened in November 1945, gives its verdicts on the Nazi leaders in 1946, and the Tokyo trials judge Japan's wartime leaders until 1948. Anne Frank's diary is published in 1947 and becomes one of the most read records of the Holocaust.
